newsitem.title: FINLAND: ECONOMISTS SAY FINNISH JAN GDP ON EXPECTED PATH.
newsitem.headline: ECONOMISTS SAY FINNISH JAN GDP ON EXPECTED PATH.

text.p: Economists on Thursday said Finland's January GDP growth rate of 5.7 percent year-on-year signalled that the economy was on track for predicted growth this year, even if the rise is from a low comparable level.
"These figures tell us much what we have expected," said OKOBANK chief economist Matti Huomo, adding that OKOBANK sees the economy growing by up to five percent this year.
"These figures show that the good pace of growth (attained at the end of last year) is continuing in the early part of 1997," Huomo said.
"This growth is both on the company side and in household consumption, so this is fairly well balanced," said economist Juha Kinnunen at the Research Institute of the Finnish Economy.
Work-day adjusted manufacturing output rose 7.5 percent year-on-year in January, Statistics Finland (SF) reported.
January construction output rose 13.5 percent year-on-year, and output in the wholesale and retail trade rose 3.5 percent.
Forestry and agricultural production was up 4.5 percent in January on January of l996. Transport and communications output increased over 10 percent year-on-year in January, SF said.
Output of other services and production by the public sector grew 2.5 percent, SF said.

With unemployment at 15.8 percent in February, the January GDP growth figures hardly point to any general overheating, but some labour shortages and materials shortages could occur in the fast-growing building sector, economists said.
"Some local-level overheating could occur," Huomo said, referring specifically to the construction industry.
"We could now see high unemployment and labour shortages simultaneously," he said.
